links.outcome: Agent performance on multi-step emergency medicine workflows with tool use
links.effect: Multi-step workflow performance collapsed to near zero (Claude 1.0%, GPT-5.4 0.0%) despite partial competence on individual steps; safety-failure rates were 27.5% and 34.0% overall.
links.quote: On multi-step workflows - the closest proxy to real emergency care - performance collapses to near zero (Claude 1.0%, GPT-5.4 0.0%) despite partial competence on individual steps.

unlisted_practices: Trajectory-level safety reward rubric that zeroes reward on any safety-critical criterion violation in an RL environment
Verifying evaluation infrastructure fidelity, since bug fixes changed which model appeared stronger
Deterministic LLM-judge overlay to bound evaluator noise
Checking reward gameability (restraint criteria) before using a benchmark as a training reward

screen.reason: The paper introduces and benchmarks HealthCraft, a simulation/RL safety evaluation environment for testing LLM agentic safety and tool use in emergency medicine workflows.
